title: Compatibility wrangler for tool calls: OpenAI tools ↔ legacy function mapping
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a runtime-level compatibility layer that reconciles OpenAI-style tool descriptors and calls with our legacy function invocation surface. The goal is to ensure predictable streaming behavior, preserve structured outputs, and avoid breaking customer contracts when routes or signatures differ. This ticket covers design, implementation of normalization rules, runtime shim, and rollout/telemetry requirements.
background: We have a growing set of customers using both OpenAI-style tool contracts (name + json schema + call metadata) and older 'legacy functions' used by earlier integrations. Recent incidents show edge cases where name mismatches and schema differences cause silent failures in streaming or incorrect structured outputs. UX and infra teams need a single shim that can perform safe name mapping, schema adaptation, and graceful fallback to preserve SLOs.
proposed_solution: Introduce a Compatibility Wrangler component in the request path that performs: 1) canonical name lookup (multi-source: alias registry + heuristics), 2) parameter normalization (type coercion + defaulting rules), 3) streaming envelope translation (map tool call events to legacy invocation stream frames), and 4) deterministic fallback policies (map to compatible model variant or return structured error with suggested mapping). The wrapper exposes a small policy config per route to allow canary rollout and per-customer overrides.
implementation_notes:
- Add an alias registry persisted in the config store with versioned entries and deprecation metadata.
- Implement a best-effort matcher using exact, namespace-aware, and fuzzy token matching (Levenshtein + token overlap) with confidence score.
- Parameter adapters run as idempotent, side-effect-free functions before handoff to existing runtime invocation.
- Streaming translation keeps token-level provenance so partial tool outputs stream to the client unchanged where possible, and structured output frames are emitted when available.
- Provide a runtime flag and route-level config to turn on/off strict validation for gradual rollout.
tradeoffs:
- Fuzzy matching reduces immediate breakage but can mask incorrect mappings and create long-term technical debt if aliases proliferate.
- Adding the shim increases request path complexity and latency; mitigate with caching and compiled match tables.
- Strict validation reduces silent errors but increases risk of breakage on upgrade; prefer opt-in strictness for enterprise routes.
rollout_plan: 1) Unit tests + integration tests in staging. 2) Deploy shim behind feature flag default-off. 3) Enable for internal dev orgs and run compatibility audit tool against production traffic for 48 hours. 4) Enable for low-traffic customer routes with monitoring. 5) Gradually increase coverage and enable strict mode where telemetry shows zero mismatches. 6) Publish deprecation mappings and allow customers 30 days to adopt canonical names.
testing:
- End-to-end test harness that replays historical toolcall traces (OpenAI-style + legacy) and validates identical client-observed outputs.
- Fuzz tests around name variations, schema mismatches, and partial streaming events.
- Performance benchmark to ensure added latency < 8ms p50 on hot paths.
- Backwards compatibility tests asserting legacy function traces still complete when shim engaged.
telemetry: Emit the following metrics and logs: shim_match_confidence (histogram), mapping_applied (count broken down by route), fallback_triggered (count + reason), streaming_frame_translation_latency (p50/p95), deprecation_warnings_emitted (count). Tag with route/model/customer and include trace_id for correlation with existing console dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility shim deployed behind feature flag and exercised by staging replay harness.
No client-visible regressions for 98% of replayed traces; remaining mismatches documented with root cause.
Latency regression on toolcall path <= 10ms p50 in synthetic benchmarks.
Telemetry surfaces mapping confidence and fallback reasons in Console and alerting configured for high fallback rate.
Migration doc published for customers describing canonical names and timeline.
Security review completed and PR merged to runtime repo.
